intuition: Compare the first and last relevant characters, then move inward. Skip punctuation and spaces, and compare letters without case differences. A mismatch proves the string is not a palindrome. If all mirrored pairs match, the normalized text reads the same in both directions.

At each side, skip characters that are not alphanumeric. The next meaningful left and right characters form the outermost unmatched pair of the normalized sequence. Compare their lowercase forms and move inward only if they agree. Digits participate like letters; a digit and an unrelated letter must not be silently ignored.

If the pointers meet or cross after punctuation skips, no unmatched pair remains. This includes a string containing only punctuation, whose normalized sequence is empty and therefore palindromic. The bounds checks inside both skip loops protect exactly this case. A single mismatch proves failure immediately, so the algorithm need not scan the remaining interior.
Each original position is visited at most once from one side, giving linear time and constant extra space.

Printable ASCII makes the character policy unambiguous. Extending the problem to Unicode would require a separate decision about case folding and normalization, since some case mappings expand to multiple code points and visually equivalent strings need not have identical encodings. The reference keeps the stated ASCII semantics.
